steps.title: Import required modules

successCriteria: The file contains no imports and is ready for writing pure JavaScript code.

steps.title: Define the function signature
steps.instruction: Create a function named 'groupBy' that takes two parameters: 'items' (an array) and 'key' (a string).
steps.hint: You can use either a function declaration or arrow function syntax. The function should be defined at the top level of your file.
steps.expectedOutcome: The function 'groupBy' is defined with the correct parameters: items and key.
successCriteria: Function 'groupBy' is defined with two parameters: items and key.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've correctly defined the function signature for groupBy.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your function is named 'groupBy' and accepts both 'items' and 'key' as parameters.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't match the required function signature. Try creating a function named 'groupBy' with parameters for items and key.

steps.title: Initialize an empty object for grouping
steps.instruction: Inside your groupBy function, declare a variable called 'grouped' and assign it an empty object.
steps.hint: You can use 'const grouped = {};' to create an empty object that will store your grouped results.
steps.expectedOutcome: Your function will have an empty object variable ready to accumulate grouped items.
successCriteria: The function contains a variable declaration 'grouped' assigned to an empty object {}.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created an empty object to store your grouped results.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've declared a variable called 'grouped' and assigned it an empty object {}.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try again. Inside the groupBy function, create a variable named 'grouped' and set it to an empty object {}.

steps.title: Start a loop through the items array
steps.instruction: Inside your groupBy function, add a for...of loop to iterate through each item in the array parameter.
steps.hint: Use the syntax: for (const item of array) { } to loop through each element in the array.
steps.expectedOutcome: The function will have a loop structure ready to process each array element.
successCriteria: A for...of loop is added inside the groupBy function that iterates through the array parameter.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added the loop structure to iterate through each item in the array.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using a for...of loop to iterate through the array parameter.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look like a for...of loop. Try using: for (const item of array) { } to iterate through the array.

steps.title: Extract the grouping key value from current item
steps.instruction: Inside the for...of loop, extract the value of the current item's property specified by the key parameter and store it in a variable named 'keyValue'.
steps.hint: Use bracket notation (item[key]) to dynamically access the property value from the current item object.
steps.expectedOutcome: The loop now contains a variable 'keyValue' that holds the value of the specified property from each item.
successCriteria: A variable named 'keyValue' is declared inside the loop and assigned the value of item[key].
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully extracted the grouping key value using bracket notation.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using bracket notation (item[key]) to access the property value dynamically.
steps.feedbackWrong: The key value extraction is missing or incorrect. Inside the loop, create a variable 'keyValue' and assign it the value of item[key].

steps.title: Check if the group key exists in the result object
steps.instruction: Inside the for loop, add an if statement to check if the extracted key value does not exist as a property in the grouped object.
steps.hint: You can use the 'in' operator or check if grouped[keyValue] is undefined to determine if the key doesn't exist yet.
steps.expectedOutcome: The function should now include a conditional check to determine if a grouping key is new or already exists in the result object.
successCriteria: An if statement is added inside the loop that checks whether the extracted key value is not already a property of the grouped object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added the conditional check to see if the grouping key is new. This is essential for handling both new and existing groups properly.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but the conditional check needs to specifically test if the key doesn't exist in the grouped object. Make sure you're checking the extracted key value against the grouped object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The conditional check for new vs existing groups is missing. Add an if statement that checks whether the extracted key value is not already a property in the grouped object.

steps.title: Initialize a new array for new group keys
steps.instruction: Inside the if block, create a new empty array in the grouped object for the current key value.
steps.hint: When a group key doesn't exist yet, you need to initialize it as an empty array in the grouped object so you can push items into it later.
steps.expectedOutcome: The grouped object will have a new property for each unique key value, initialized as an empty array.
successCriteria: Inside the if block, grouped[keyValue] is assigned an empty array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've initialized a new empty array for the current key value. This prepares the grouped object to receive items for this group.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're assigning an empty array to grouped[keyValue] inside the if block.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. When the key doesn't exist in grouped, you need to create a new property with that key and set its value to an empty array.

steps.title: Push the current item into its group array
steps.instruction: After the if block, push the current item into the array corresponding to its key in the grouped object.
steps.hint: Use the push method on the array stored at grouped[keyValue] to add the current item.
steps.expectedOutcome: The function should now add each item to its corresponding group array during the loop.
successCriteria: The code includes a statement that pushes the current item into the appropriate array in the grouped object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the item to its group array. The grouping logic is now building up the arrays with matching items.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're pushing the current item (the 'item' variable) into the array at grouped[keyValue].
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. After checking if the group exists, you need to add the current item to that group's array using the push method.

steps.title: Return the grouped result object
steps.instruction: After the loop, add a return statement to return the grouped object from the function.
steps.hint: Use the return keyword followed by the variable that holds your grouped object.
steps.expectedOutcome: The function should now return the grouped object after processing all items.
successCriteria: The function returns the grouped object using a return statement
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the return statement. The function now returns the grouped object after processing all items.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're returning the grouped object from the function after the loop ends.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function should return the grouped object after processing all items. Add a return statement with the grouped variable.

steps.title: Test the function with sample data
steps.instruction: Add sample data and call the groupBy function, then log the result to the console.
steps.hint: Create an array of objects with a common property, call groupBy with that array and property name, and use console.log to see the output.
steps.expectedOutcome: The console will display the grouped object: { fruit: [{ category: 'fruit', name: 'apple' }, { category: 'fruit', name: 'banana' }], vegetable: [{ category: 'vegetable', name: 'carrot' }] }.
successCriteria: The sampleData array is defined, groupBy is called with sampleData and 'category', and the result is logged to console.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully tested the groupBy function with sample data and verified its output.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some test code, but ensure you define sampleData, call groupBy with the correct arguments, and log the result.
steps.feedbackWrong: The test code is missing or incorrect. Define a sample array, call groupBy with it and a key, then log the result.
